Q2 (h05): When a user is deleted, are their emoji reactions removed by (a) explicit Go code in the DeleteUser store method or a service layer, (b) a database-level rule (ON DELETE CASCADE in schema migrations), or (c) not at all? Check the DeleteUser implementations in store/db/sqlite, mysql, postgres; check the reaction table schema in migration files for foreign keys/cascade; check any user-deletion service code. Report the mechanism and every location you checked with path:line.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## Q1: Is `mysql.NewDB` constructed outside the factory?

**No.** The MySQL driver constructor is called in exactly one place in the entire repo.

- Constructor definition: `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20` — `func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error)`, returning `&driver` (a `*DB`) at `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:39`.
- **Only call site (the factory):** `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:22` — inside `NewDBDriver` (`/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:14`), in the `case "mysql":` branch of the driver-selection switch.

Grep evidence (`mysql\.NewDB|postgres\.NewDB|sqlite\.NewDB` across all `.go` files, tests included):
- `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:20` — `sqlite.NewDB` (factory)
- `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:22` — `mysql.NewDB` (factory)
- `/bench/repo/store/db/db.go:24` — `postgres.NewDB` (factory)
- `/bench/repo/store/demo_seed_test.go:24` — `sqlite.NewDB` (TEST, sqlite only)
- `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config_test.go:416` — `sqlite.NewDB` (TEST, sqlite only)

So sqlite has two direct test-side bypasses of the factory, but MySQL has **zero** outside `db.go:22`.

Related near-misses I ruled out:
- `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12` — `db := &DB{}` — a zero-value struct literal inside the `mysql` package's own unit test (no DSN/connection, not a `NewDB` call). Same pattern for postgres at `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/auth_config_test.go:12` and `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_setting_test.go:36,194,257`.
- `/bench/repo/store/test/containers.go:101-105` — `mysql.Run(...)`, but that is the **testcontainers** `modules/mysql` package, not the store driver package.
- All test harness paths go through the factory: `/bench/repo/store/test/store.go:28`, `/bench/repo/store/test/store.go:50`, `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:70` all call `db.NewDBDriver`.

## Q2: How are a deleted user's reactions removed?

**Mechanism (a): explicit Go code in the per-driver `DeleteUser` store method.** There is no database-level cascade — the `reaction` table has no foreign keys at all.

### Explicit deletion code (two separate DELETEs per driver, inside one transaction)

Each driver's `deleteUserTargetsTx` runs both a content-based and a creator-based reaction delete:

- SQLite: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`) and `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:102` (`deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`); implementations at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:380-388` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN (...)`, batched at 500) and `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:400-403` (`DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?`).
- MySQL: `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:96` and `:102`; implementations at `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:417-420` and `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:437-438`.
- Postgres: `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:96` and `:102`; implementations at `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:380-383` and `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:400-401`.

Semantics: the content-ID pass removes *all* reactions (including other users') on the deleted user's memo subtree — content IDs built as `"memos/"+memo.UID` at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:512-518`; the creator pass removes the deleted user's own reactions on *other* people's memos. Entry points: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`, `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:29`, `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:29` — all wrapped in a single `BeginTx`/`Commit` so reaction removal is atomic with the user row delete (`deleteUserRowTx`, `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:461`).

### Not a DB cascade — schema evidence

The `reaction` table is declared with no `FOREIGN KEY` clause in any dialect:
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`
- `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`
- Original creation migrations, also FK-free: `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2`

The only `ON DELETE CASCADE` remaining in current schema is on `memo_share.memo_id -> memo(id)`: `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:108`, `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:108` (added in `/bench/repo/store/migration/*/0.27/04__memo_share.sql:11`). Historic user-cascade FKs existed in old sqlite migrations (`/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/0.5/00__regenerate_foreign_keys.sql:59,97,98,125,167,204`) but were dropped by `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/0.7/00__remove_fk.sql:1`. Even if FKs existed, SQLite runs with them disabled: `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:53` opens with `_pragma=foreign_keys(0)`, documented at `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:40`.

### Service / store layers (no extra reaction logic)

- `/bench/repo/store/user.go:171-181` — `Store.DeleteUser` just delegates to `s.driver.DeleteUser` then `s.deleteUserCache` (`/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go:39`). No reaction handling; cache layer touches no reaction cache.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:393` — `APIV1Service.DeleteUser` handles permissions, then calls `s.Store.DeleteUser` and afterwards only cleans up attachment blob storage and auth cookies. No reaction code.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go:138` — thin Connect wrapper over the above.

### Test coverage confirming behavior

- `/bench/repo/store/test/user_delete_test.go:97-113` seeds three reactions, and `:217-220` asserts a peer's reaction on a peer memo survives while the deleted user's are gone.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/user_service_delete_test.go:188-209` and assertions at `:287-298` (own-memo and own-comment reactions empty; the peer's reaction on a foreign memo preserved), plus rollback coverage at `:366-369` / `:429-431` confirming the reaction survives a failed transaction.
